clue.text: Played 24, but didn't play fair

definitions.meaning: 24 refers to the answer at 24-down, so this reads 'played tunes', as on a violin
cheated, as with doctored accounts or a crooked deal

explanation.surface: Someone performed a piece but cheated in doing so.
explanation.walkthrough: The cross-reference sends you to 24-down; once that is in, 'Played 24' means played on a violin in the casual sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Playing tunes on a violin and cheating by swindling are both everyday senses of the one verb.

clue.text: Clash about servicemen's transportation

indicators.note: about means the word for clash goes round the servicemen

parts.note: a clash is a fight
RE, the Royal Engineers, are British Army servicemen

explanation.surface: A dispute over how soldiers are to be moved.
explanation.walkthrough: RE is the Royal Engineers, a corps of the British Army.
explanation.definitionFit: Goods carried by lorry, ship or rail are cargo, the thing being transported.

clue.text: Diana's stayed put out

parts.note: Di is short for Diana, and the 's adds an S
to lodge is to stay as a guest or tenant

explanation.surface: Diana stayed put but was moved on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stayed put' looks like one phrase, but 'put out' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To be removed from a fixed place is to be shifted or ejected.

clue.text: These days none put up 'a woman

indicators.note: in a down clue put up means the pieces are read from the bottom upward

parts.note: AD, Anno Domini, marks the present era
nil means none

explanation.surface: Nowadays nobody takes in a lady lodger.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put up' turns ADNIL to give the girl's name.
explanation.definitionFit: A common female first name, so an example of a woman.

clue.text: A set creed could appear' profane'.

indicators.note: could appear suggests the letters a set creed might show up in another order

explanation.surface: A fixed doctrine might seem irreverent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'could appear' signals rearranging A SET CREED; 'profane' is a verb here.
explanation.definitionFit: To violate something sacred is to treat it with irreverence, a verb sense of the definition.

clue.text: William was back first, being a flier

indicators.note: first says the turned word comes before the name in the answer
back tells us the word was is read in the opposite direction

parts.note: Bill is the familiar short form of William

explanation.surface: William once went first, as if he were an airman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns WAS into SAW, and 'first' puts that ahead of BILL.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a fish-eating duck with a serrated beak, a merganser, so a bird that flies.

clue.text: Cut, but not completely disheartened by it

indicators.note: not completely means only a run from inside disheartened is used

explanation.surface: Somebody was cut, though not wholly put off by it.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters sit in the middle of 'disheartened'.
explanation.definitionFit: To clip fleece from a sheep or trim with large blades is to cut.

clue.text: Jet base' supplied with everything required

parts.note: to well is to gush or spurt like a jet
to found is to base or ground something

explanation.surface: An airfield equipped with all it needs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jet base' suggests an airfield; the two words are split.
explanation.definitionFit: A ship or house that is fully equipped and furnished has all it needs.

clue.text: State one had to turn round

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: to turn means the word had is read the other way

parts.note: O is round in shape

explanation.surface: A country in which someone had to turn about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to turn' turns HAD into DAH; 'round' gives the ring-shaped O.
explanation.definitionFit: A US state in the north-west, known for potatoes.

clue.text: Without cover the trainee doesn't work hard — point taken!

parts.note: L is the learner plate on a trainee driver's car
idles means does little or no work
S, south, is a point of the compass

explanation.surface: A slack learner gets the message.
explanation.walkthrough: 'point taken' sounds like agreement but adds S, a compass point.
explanation.definitionFit: Having no lid or top means being uncovered.

clue.text: German township enters, .nevertheless

annotationWithheld.why: German township enters, nevertheless (5) for ESSEN: the scan prints it so, and no reading of 'enters, nevertheless' gives the letters; a search found no parse

clue.text: Delay rest, perhaps, to find' the balance

indicators.note: perhaps suggests the letters of delay rest may be arranged some other way

explanation.surface: Putting off a break in order to reach a fair equilibrium.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' signals rearranging the nine letters of DELAY REST.
explanation.definitionFit: A steelyard is an old weighing device with a sliding weight on a long arm, a kind of scale.

clue.text: An earthy forecaster!

parts.note: not a coarse weatherman but a fortune-teller whose divination works by reading soil, sand or marks on the ground

explanation.surface: A weather prophet with a crude, down-to-earth manner.
explanation.definitionFit: Divination from patterns in earth or scattered soil is the craft named by the Greek word for earth plus prophecy.

clue.text: A priest given short weight by Oriental turned quite cold

parts.note: Fr, short for Father, is the title of a Catholic priest
oz is the abbreviated form of ounce, a unit of weight
E stands for East, so Oriental gives E

explanation.surface: A cleric is cheated on weight by an Easterner and goes cold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short weight' is not cheating but the abbreviation OZ.
explanation.definitionFit: To freeze in the past tense is to have become icy, chilled through.

clue.text: Not'; relaxed, having drunk rather 'too much

explanation.surface: Someone who is far from relaxed after one drink too many.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses belong to the one adjective: taut as a rope, and informally tipsy or inebriated.

clue.text: Frustrating article about disfigurement

indicators.note: about means the word for article goes round the disfigurement

parts.note: an article is a thing, an object
a wart is a small growth that spoils the skin

explanation.surface: A piece about a facial blemish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'article' looks like A or THE but is THING.
explanation.definitionFit: Blocking or foiling someone's plans is frustrating them.

clue.text: Gunmen who throve before Agincourt (Hen. V)

definitions.text: Gunmen who throve before Agincourt (Hen. V)

parts.words: Gunmen who throve before Agincourt (Hen. V)
parts.note: the Chorus in Shakespeare's Henry V says 'Now thrive' the makers of weapons and armour as England prepares for war; gunmen here means men who make arms

explanation.surface: A historical note about armed men prospering before a famous battle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gunmen' suggests shooters, but these are the craftsmen who made and fitted weapons and armour; the line is from the Act 2 Chorus of Henry V.
explanation.definitionFit: These craftsmen made weapons and plate for soldiers, so they prospered as the army readied for France.

clue.text: She'll find a trim figure lacking in early spring!

indicators.note: in means the shortened phrase goes inside the spring month

parts.note: March is the first month of spring

indicators.note: lacking means the figure is removed from a trim

parts.note: M is the Roman numeral for 1,000, a figure

explanation.surface: Someone without a slim build discovering it at the start of spring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lacking' takes M from A TRIM to leave ATRI, which goes 'in' MARCH after the M.
explanation.definitionFit: She will be the female head of a family, the definition taken as a pronoun for that woman.

clue.text: A complaint as regards attendants.

parts.note: to regard is to look at, so regards means eyes as a verb
a train is a retinue of followers

explanation.surface: A grievance concerning servants.
explanation.walkthrough: 'as regards' looks like 'concerning', but regards is a verb meaning looks at.
explanation.definitionFit: Tiredness of the sight from overuse is a minor ailment.

clue.text: Sort of gift women tend to make

indicators.note: to make here means the letters of women tend are worked into a new word

explanation.surface: A kind of present that women are inclined to give.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to make' signals rearranging WOMEN TEND, which looks like part of a sentence about habits.
explanation.definitionFit: A bequest or donation of money to fund an institution is a gift of a particular kind.

clue.text: Rent arranged with social worker, he moves in

indicators.note: arranged means the letters of rent are put in a new order

parts.note: an ant is a social insect, a worker in its colony

explanation.surface: A rental fixed up through a care worker for someone moving in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'social worker' is a classic crossword trick for ANT.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who joins a contest or comes into a place is a newcomer who goes in.

clue.text: Getting a large number back can …be dispiriting

parts.note: D is the Roman numeral for 500, a large number
the rear of something is its back

explanation.surface: Receiving a big total in return could be depressing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' looks like a reversal signal but is simply REAR.
explanation.definitionFit: This poetic adjective means gloomy and dreary, so depressing.

clue.text: Note about Conservative minister's address

parts.note: re is the second note of the sol-fa scale
c, circa, means about
a Tory is a member of the UK Conservative Party

explanation.surface: A memo concerning where a Tory government minister lives.
explanation.walkthrough: 'minister' is a clergyman, not a politician.
explanation.definitionFit: The house provided for a parish clergyman is his home.

clue.text: The sailor sheltered by a rocky height, a mountain

indicators.note: sheltered by means the sailor is placed within the rocky height

parts.note: a tor is a rocky hilltop, as on Dartmoor
AB, able seaman, is the usual crossword sailor

explanation.surface: A seaman takes shelter beneath a crag on a mountainside.
explanation.walkthrough: A TOR is a craggy hill top, common on the moors of south-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: Mount Tabor is a hill in Galilee, traditionally the site of the Transfiguration.

clue.text: Stick to going in the bar

indicators.note: going in means the word to is placed inside the bar

parts.note: to bar is to ban

explanation.surface: Stay in the pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bar' looks like a pub, but it means BAN.
explanation.definitionFit: A short rod held by a conductor or relay runner is a stick.

clue.text: Man after a kiss'- a jerk, that's self-evident!

indicators.note: after places Man behind the letters for a kiss

parts.note: X is the kiss at the end of a letter
IOM is the abbreviation for the Isle of Man
a tic is an involuntary twitch or jerk

explanation.surface: A man comes after a kiss and behaves like a fool, which is obvious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Man' is not a person but the Isle of Man, abbreviated IOM; 'jerk' is a twitch, not an idiot.
explanation.definitionFit: Something taken as a basic truth needing no proof is obvious in itself.

clue.text: A firm check by all accounts

definitions.text: A firm check by all accounts

parts.words: A firm check by all accounts
parts.note: a thorough examination of a company's books, going through every one of its records

explanation.surface: A rigorous test, as everyone reports.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by all accounts' looks like 'reportedly' but means across every account.
explanation.definitionFit: An official inspection of a company's financial records is a check on the firm.

clue.text: The greatest good that mortals know, according to Addison

definitions.text: The greatest good that mortals know, according to Addison

parts.words: The greatest good that mortals know, according to Addison
parts.note: a line from Joseph Addison's Song for St Cecilia's Day, praising the art of tunes and harmony

explanation.surface: A quotation from the essayist Addison about the highest human good.
explanation.definitionFit: Addison's ode for the patron saint of musicians calls the art of melody the greatest good mortals know.

clue.text: Gain communistic backing as a result of treasonable activity

parts.note: to attain is to gain or achieve

indicators.note: backing says the word for communistic is read from the end

parts.note: red is the colour and byword for communism

explanation.surface: Winning support from the Left leads to a charge of treason.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' looks like support but turns RED into DER after ATTAIN.
explanation.definitionFit: Historically, conviction for treason brought loss of civil rights and forfeiture of estate, known by this legal term.

clue.text: Capital investment for a soldier at one time

definitions.text: Capital investment for a soldier at one time

parts.words: Capital investment for a soldier at one time
parts.note: capital means head and investment means clothing, so this is a hat once worn by troops, not money put into a firm

explanation.surface: Money put into a business on behalf of an old soldier.
explanation.walkthrough: Old crossword sense: to invest is to clothe, and the capital is the head.
explanation.definitionFit: This tall, peaked military cap with a plume was worn by infantry in the nineteenth century.

clue.text: Today's dark, so a child will keep 'near

indicators.note: will keep means the child holds the word for near inside it

parts.note: a tot is a small child
nigh is an old word for near

explanation.surface: It is dark now, so a little one will stay close by.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Today's dark' is the definition, the evening of this day.
explanation.definitionFit: The coming evening, the dark part of the present day, is this one word.

clue.text: Marshy place for a carriage

definitions.meaning: ... Marshes is a large stretch of open land in east London famous for Sunday football
a horse-drawn carriage for hire, the forerunner of the London cab

explanation.surface: A boggy spot where you might find a coach.
explanation.walkthrough: HACKNEY is a borough of east London; its Marshes are well known.
explanation.definitionFit: The London district gives its name to the marshes, and a horse-drawn vehicle for hire shares the name.
